project-charter.title: 1. Engineering Problem Charter & Technical Scope

cards.title: Industrial Comparative Scenario & Transmission Brief
cards.body: In mechanical power transmission engineering, selecting the appropriate gear technology is a decisive architectural decision. An industrial transmission design engineer must determine when to employ straight external Spur Gears and when to select inclined Helical Gears. This comparative challenge evaluates side-by-side parallel-shaft transmissions across kinematic, mechanical, tribological, manufacturing, dynamic, and economic dimensions.

cards.title: Syllabus Boundary & Regulatory Scope (SPPU PCC353-MEC)
cards.body: In accordance with the SPPU PCC353-MEC syllabus (Unit I — Spur and Helical Gears), this assignment focuses on the comparative engineering principles of power transmission. The syllabus explicitly mandates: 'No numerical on force analysis of helical'. Consequently, helical gear force characteristics (tangential Ft, radial Fr, and axial thrust Fa) are evaluated conceptually, vectorially, and directionally. Students are not required to perform numerical helical force or thrust calculations.

cards.title: Professional Decision Responsibility
cards.body: The choice between spur and helical gears directly dictates bearing selection, casing rigidity, acoustic emissions, vibration levels, lubrication requirements, and initial manufacturing costs. Recommending an unsuitable gear type can cause excessive noise, premature bearing failure, or unnecessary capital expenditure. The design engineer must justify their technical selection with rigorous mechanical reasoning.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I have reviewed the Transmission Comparative Charter and understand that I must evaluate tooth engagement kinematics, 3D force characteristics, bearing arrangements, dynamic behavior, manufacturing trade-offs, and industrial application requirements without numerical helical force calculations under PCC353-MEC (CO1).

gear-type-identification.title: 3. Gear-Type Identification & Geometric Architecture
gear-type-identification.description: Analyze the architectural and geometric parameters distinguishing spur gears from helical gears.

questions.prompt: How are the tooth traces oriented relative to the shaft axis in spur versus helical gears?
options: Spur: tooth trace is parallel to the shaft axis; Helical: tooth trace is inclined along a cylindrical helix at angle beta
Spur: tooth trace is inclined at 45°; Helical: tooth trace is strictly parallel to the axis
Both spur and helical teeth have identical tooth trace orientations parallel to the shaft axis
Spur: curved cycloidal trace; Helical: straight radial line intersecting at right angles
questions.correctAnswer: Spur: tooth trace is parallel to the shaft axis; Helical: tooth trace is inclined along a cylindrical helix at angle beta
questions.explanation: Spur gear teeth are cut straight and parallel to the axis of rotation. Helical gear teeth wind around the pitch cylinder at a constant helix angle beta.

questions.prompt: In standard design nomenclature (Bhandari / SPPU), what is the relationship between normal module (mn) and transverse module (mt) in helical gears?
options: mt = mn / cos(beta)
mt = mn * cos(beta)
mt = mn / sin(beta)
mt = mn * tan(beta)
questions.correctAnswer: mt = mn / cos(beta)
questions.explanation: Because the normal plane is inclined at helix angle beta, the circular pitch in the transverse plane is larger: pt = pn / cos(beta), which yields mt = mn / cos(beta).

questions.prompt: How are the pressure angles in the normal plane (alpha_n) and transverse plane (alpha_t) related for a helical gear?
options: tan(alpha_t) = tan(alpha_n) / cos(beta)
tan(alpha_t) = tan(alpha_n) * cos(beta)
alpha_t = alpha_n * cos(beta)
alpha_t is always identical to alpha_n regardless of helix angle
questions.correctAnswer: tan(alpha_t) = tan(alpha_n) / cos(beta)
questions.explanation: Standard cutter tools have standard normal pressure angle alpha_n (usually 20°). In the transverse plane of rotation, tan(alpha_t) = tan(alpha_n) / cos(beta).

questions.prompt: What is the formative (virtual) number of teeth (z') for a helical gear with actual teeth z and helix angle beta?
options: z' = z / cos^3(beta)
z' = z * cos^3(beta)
z' = z / cos(beta)
z' = z / sin^2(beta)
questions.correctAnswer: z' = z / cos^3(beta)
questions.explanation: The virtual number of teeth z' corresponds to an equivalent spur gear constructed in the normal plane with radius of curvature r' = r / cos^2(beta), yielding z' = z / cos^3(beta).

tooth-engagement-kinematics.title: 4. Tooth Engagement Kinematics & Contact Line Mechanics
tooth-engagement-kinematics.description: Examine the contact line progression and meshing kinematics of straight spur teeth versus inclined helical teeth.

questions.prompt: Describe the tooth engagement action of a straight spur gear pair as a pair of teeth comes into mesh:
options: Initial contact occurs as an instantaneous line contact across the entire active face width simultaneously, producing a sudden impact
Initial contact occurs as a point contact that slowly spreads diagonally across the face
Initial contact begins at the center of the face width and radiates outward in both directions
Engagement is purely sliding without any line contact across the face width
questions.correctAnswer: Initial contact occurs as an instantaneous line contact across the entire active face width simultaneously, producing a sudden impact
questions.explanation: Because spur teeth are straight and parallel to the axis, the entire tooth face engages all at once along a full-width line of contact, creating cyclic impact excitation.

questions.prompt: Describe how tooth engagement progresses across the face width in a helical gear pair:
options: Contact begins at a point at the leading edge of the tooth and extends diagonally across the face width as rotation proceeds, providing gradual and progressive load transfer
Contact occurs abruptly across the full face width exactly like a spur gear
Contact occurs only at the exact midpoint of the tooth face throughout meshing
Contact occurs along the root fillet first before reaching the tooth flank
questions.correctAnswer: Contact begins at a point at the leading edge of the tooth and extends diagonally across the face width as rotation proceeds, providing gradual and progressive load transfer
questions.explanation: The inclined tooth trace causes engagement to commence at the leading tip and progress smoothly and diagonally across the face width, avoiding sudden shock loading.

questions.prompt: How does the tooth contact line geometry differ between spur and helical gears during the meshing cycle?
options: Spur: contact line is parallel to the shaft axis; Helical: contact lines are inclined diagonally across the tooth flank
Spur: contact lines are circular; Helical: contact lines are straight vertical lines
Spur: diagonal lines; Helical: lines parallel to the shaft axis
Both gear types have identical contact lines parallel to the shaft axis
questions.correctAnswer: Spur: contact line is parallel to the shaft axis; Helical: contact lines are inclined diagonally across the tooth flank
questions.explanation: In spur gears, the line of contact is straight and parallel to the gear axis. In helical gears, the contact line is inclined at an angle across the tooth surface.

questions.prompt: What is the primary dynamic consequence of progressive tooth engagement in helical gears compared to sudden impact in spur gears?
options: Significantly smoother tooth meshing, reduced dynamic impact excitation, lower vibration levels, and substantially quieter operation
Higher dynamic impact excitation and increased acoustic gear chatter
Complete elimination of friction between meshing teeth
Lower load capacity because multiple teeth cannot share load
questions.correctAnswer: Significantly smoother tooth meshing, reduced dynamic impact excitation, lower vibration levels, and substantially quieter operation
questions.explanation: Progressive load transfer prevents sudden load spikes, drastically suppressing vibration and gear whine even at elevated operating speeds.

force-characteristics.title: 5. Force Characteristics & 3D Force Vector Resolution
force-characteristics.description: Analyze the 2D planar forces of spur gears and the 3D spatial forces of helical gears.

questions.prompt: What are the force components acting on a straight spur gear tooth in mesh?
options: Tangential force (Ft) which transmits torque, Radial force (Fr) which tends to separate the shafts, and Zero axial force (Fa = 0)
Tangential force (Ft), Radial force (Fr), and a large Axial thrust force (Fa)
Tangential force (Ft) and Axial thrust force (Fa) only, with Zero radial force
Purely axial force (Fa) with zero tangential force
questions.correctAnswer: Tangential force (Ft) which transmits torque, Radial force (Fr) which tends to separate the shafts, and Zero axial force (Fa = 0)
questions.explanation: Spur gear tooth forces act entirely in the 2D transverse plane perpendicular to the shaft axis: Ft = 2T/d and Fr = Ft*tan(alpha). There is zero axial component (Fa = 0).

questions.prompt: What are the force components acting on a helical gear tooth in 3D spatial resolution?
options: Tangential force (Ft) transmitting torque, Radial separating force (Fr), and an Axial thrust force (Fa) acting parallel to the shaft axis
Tangential force (Ft) and Radial force (Fr) only, with zero axial thrust
Axial thrust force (Fa) only, with zero radial and tangential forces
Centrifugal force and gyroscopic precession force only
questions.correctAnswer: Tangential force (Ft) transmitting torque, Radial separating force (Fr), and an Axial thrust force (Fa) acting parallel to the shaft axis
questions.explanation: Because the tooth surface is inclined at helix angle beta, the normal resultant force resolves into three mutually perpendicular 3D components: Ft, Fr, and Fa.

questions.prompt: What is the physical origin and governing relationship of the axial thrust force (Fa) in helical gears?
options: It arises from the tooth helix inclination angle beta, governed conceptually by Fa = Ft * tan(beta)
It arises from friction between tooth surfaces, governed by Fa = mu * Fr
It arises from shaft deflection under bending loads, governed by Fa = Ft / cos(beta)
It arises from centrifugal force acting on the gear rim at high rotational speeds
questions.correctAnswer: It arises from the tooth helix inclination angle beta, governed conceptually by Fa = Ft * tan(beta)
questions.explanation: The tooth surface normal is angled by helix angle beta relative to the transverse plane. Resolving vectors along the shaft axis gives Fa = Ft * tan(beta).

questions.prompt: What determines the direction of the axial thrust force (Fa) on a helical gear shaft?
options: The combination of the helix hand (Right-Hand vs Left-Hand), the role (Driving pinion vs Driven gear), and the direction of shaft rotation
Only the magnitude of transmitted motor power, independent of helix hand
Only the gear diameter ratio, independent of rotation direction
The axial thrust always acts towards the motor regardless of helix hand or rotation
questions.correctAnswer: The combination of the helix hand (Right-Hand vs Left-Hand), the role (Driving pinion vs Driven gear), and the direction of shaft rotation
questions.explanation: Using the right-hand / left-hand rule, reversing shaft rotation or changing helix hand reverses the direction of the axial thrust vector along the shaft axis.

bearing-consequences.title: 6. Bearing Consequences & Shaft Mounting Integration
bearing-consequences.description: Evaluate the mechanical consequences of tooth forces on bearing selection and gearbox casing design.

questions.prompt: What bearing types are generally suitable and economical for supporting shafts in a spur gear drive?
options: Standard Deep-Groove Ball Bearings or Cylindrical Roller Bearings, because the gear forces are predominantly radial (Fa = 0)
Double-row heavy spherical roller thrust bearings are mandatory because of high axial loads
Four-point contact thrust bearings at both ends of every shaft
Fluid dynamic tilting-pad thrust bearings
questions.correctAnswer: Standard Deep-Groove Ball Bearings or Cylindrical Roller Bearings, because the gear forces are predominantly radial (Fa = 0)
questions.explanation: Spur gears produce no axial thrust (Fa = 0). Bearings only need to carry radial loads (Fr and resultant shaft bending moments), making standard radial bearings ideal.

questions.prompt: Why do helical gear shafts require thrust-capable bearing arrangements?
options: Because the helix angle generates a continuous axial thrust force (Fa) that must be reacted through the bearings into the gearbox housing
Because helical gears produce zero radial load and purely axial load
Because helical gears operate only at sub-zero temperatures requiring special bearing grease
Because helical gears have no keyways and rely on bearing friction to prevent spinning
questions.correctAnswer: Because the helix angle generates a continuous axial thrust force (Fa) that must be reacted through the bearings into the gearbox housing
questions.explanation: Helical axial thrust Fa acts parallel to the shaft axis. Without thrust-capable bearings (or opposed thrust pairs), the shaft would shift axially out of mesh.

questions.prompt: Which bearing configurations are commonly selected in industrial gearboxes to support helical gear shafts carrying combined radial and axial loads?
options: Tapered Roller Bearings in opposed arrangements (back-to-back or face-to-face), or Angular Contact Ball Bearing pairs
Pure needle roller radial bearings with loose axial clearance
Non-locating cylindrical roller bearings at both ends of the shaft
Linear ball bushings
questions.correctAnswer: Tapered Roller Bearings in opposed arrangements (back-to-back or face-to-face), or Angular Contact Ball Bearing pairs
questions.explanation: Tapered roller bearings and angular contact ball bearings have steep contact angles designed specifically to absorb combined heavy radial loads and unidirectional axial thrust.

questions.prompt: What additional design and manufacturing requirements does the presence of helical axial thrust impose on the gearbox housing?
options: Heavier housing walls and end-covers with rigid axial retention (locknuts, retaining shoulders, shims) to prevent axial deflection and parasitic friction loss
No special requirements; the housing can be made of thin, flexible sheet metal
The gearbox housing must be mounted on loose rubber springs to allow free axial sliding
Bearing retainers must be completely omitted to permit axial floating of both shafts
questions.correctAnswer: Heavier housing walls and end-covers with rigid axial retention (locknuts, retaining shoulders, shims) to prevent axial deflection and parasitic friction loss
questions.explanation: Axial thrust loads react against the casing end-caps. Housing walls must be sufficiently rigid to avoid axial deflection that would distort tooth contact alignment.

dynamic-transmission-behaviour.title: 7. Dynamic Transmission Behaviour, Noise & Velocity Limits
dynamic-transmission-behaviour.description: Compare operating speed capability, contact ratio, and acoustic performance between the two gear systems.

questions.prompt: How does contact ratio differ between spur gears and helical gears?
options: Spur gears have only transverse contact ratio (epsilon_alpha, typically 1.2 to 1.7); Helical gears have total contact ratio epsilon_gamma = epsilon_alpha + epsilon_beta (typically 2.5 to 3.5+)
Spur gears have much higher contact ratio than helical gears because their teeth are straight
Both spur and helical gears have an identical contact ratio of exactly 1.0
Helical gears have zero overlap contact ratio because of tooth inclination
questions.correctAnswer: Spur gears have only transverse contact ratio (epsilon_alpha, typically 1.2 to 1.7); Helical gears have total contact ratio epsilon_gamma = epsilon_alpha + epsilon_beta (typically 2.5 to 3.5+)
questions.explanation: In helical gears, the face overlap ratio epsilon_beta = (b * sin(beta)) / (pi * mn) adds to the transverse contact ratio, ensuring continuous multi-tooth load sharing.

questions.prompt: What is the typical pitch-line velocity operating domain for standard commercial spur gears versus precision helical gears?
options: Spur gears are best suited for low-to-moderate speeds (v < 8–10 m/s); Helical gears operate smoothly and reliably at higher speeds (v > 10–30+ m/s)
Spur gears are used exclusively above 50 m/s; Helical gears are restricted to hand-cranked mechanisms below 1 m/s
Both gear types have identical dynamic limits and fail at exactly 5 m/s
Velocity has no effect on gear noise, dynamic loading, or tooth failure
questions.correctAnswer: Spur gears are best suited for low-to-moderate speeds (v < 8–10 m/s); Helical gears operate smoothly and reliably at higher speeds (v > 10–30+ m/s)
questions.explanation: At speeds above 8–10 m/s, cyclic impact in spur gears causes severe noise and dynamic load spikes. Helical gears maintain smooth engagement at much higher velocities.

questions.prompt: How does the Barth velocity factor (Cv) reflect the dynamic superiority of precision helical gears over commercial spur gears at elevated speeds?
options: Precision helical gears maintain a significantly higher Cv factor (e.g., 5.6 / (5.6 + sqrt(v))), reducing dynamic load amplification compared to commercial cut spur gears (e.g., 3 / (3 + v) or 4.5 / (4.5 + v))
Commercial spur gears have a higher Cv than helical gears at all speeds
The Barth velocity factor increases to infinity as velocity increases
Cv is completely independent of pitch-line velocity for both gear types
questions.correctAnswer: Precision helical gears maintain a significantly higher Cv factor (e.g., 5.6 / (5.6 + sqrt(v))), reducing dynamic load amplification compared to commercial cut spur gears (e.g., 3 / (3 + v) or 4.5 / (4.5 + v))
questions.explanation: Because Peff = (Ka * Km * Ft) / Cv, a higher Cv factor means lower dynamic load penalty, allowing helical gears to transmit greater power in a compact envelope.

questions.prompt: Why are helical gears almost universally chosen over spur gears in enclosed high-speed industrial drives and passenger automotive transmissions?
options: Because their continuous multi-tooth overlap drastically reduces gear whine, acoustic noise (< 75 dBA), and high-frequency vibration
Because helical gears require no lubrication and never wear out
Because helical gears are much cheaper to manufacture than spur gears
Because helical gears generate no heat during operation
questions.correctAnswer: Because their continuous multi-tooth overlap drastically reduces gear whine, acoustic noise (< 75 dBA), and high-frequency vibration
questions.explanation: Acoustic comfort and vibration suppression are critical in automotive transmissions and plant environments; progressive helical meshing satisfies strict noise standards.

manufacturing-and-maintenance.title: 8. Manufacturing Processes, Capital Cost & Maintenance
manufacturing-and-maintenance.description: Analyze tooling, capital investment, assembly tolerances, and field maintenance trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Why are spur gears simpler and less expensive to manufacture than helical gears?
options: Spur teeth require simple straight-axis hobbing or shaping with standard tooling; they require no helix lead generation, workhead swiveling, or differential gear trains
Spur gears can be cut with handheld woodworking tools without machines
Spur gears do not require steel and can be made of unmachined timber
Spur gears require only 1 tooth to be cut, while helical gears require all teeth
questions.correctAnswer: Spur teeth require simple straight-axis hobbing or shaping with standard tooling; they require no helix lead generation, workhead swiveling, or differential gear trains
questions.explanation: Cutting helical teeth requires a synchronized rotary feed and helical lead guide, complicating machine tool kinematics and increasing initial tooling costs.

questions.prompt: How does axial alignment sensitivity compare between spur and helical gear assemblies?
options: Spur gears are relatively forgiving of slight axial displacement; Helical gears are highly sensitive to axial position and lead alignment because axial shifts alter tooth contact across the face width
Spur gears cannot tolerate even 0.001 mm of axial position; Helical gears require zero axial alignment
Both gear types are completely insensitive to shaft misalignment and tooth runout
Helical gears automatically correct any angular misalignment by twisting the shaft
questions.correctAnswer: Spur gears are relatively forgiving of slight axial displacement; Helical gears are highly sensitive to axial position and lead alignment because axial shifts alter tooth contact across the face width
questions.explanation: Because helical teeth are angled, any axial shift or lead error causes localized edge contact and uneven load distribution across the face width.

questions.prompt: What is the primary maintenance and replacement advantage of an industrial spur gear drive?
options: Lower replacement cost, readily available standard radial bearings, and straightforward field assembly without complex bearing preloading (shimming)
Spur gears never require oil changes or visual inspection
Spur gear teeth can be repaired in the field with a hammer without disassembling the casing
Spur gears have infinite fatigue life regardless of load
questions.correctAnswer: Lower replacement cost, readily available standard radial bearings, and straightforward field assembly without complex bearing preloading (shimming)
questions.explanation: Spur gear drives utilize off-the-shelf radial bearings and standard spur gears, simplifying maintenance and minimizing downtime in remote or heavy-duty plant sites.

questions.prompt: Under what condition is the higher capital expenditure of a helical gear drive fully economically justified?
options: When high operating speed, strict acoustic noise limits, or high torque density make smooth continuous engagement and reduced dynamic loading essential for transmission reliability
Only when the gearbox is run backwards at zero rpm
Whenever the plant manager wants the most expensive equipment regardless of operating parameters
Only when the transmitted power is less than 0.1 kW
questions.correctAnswer: When high operating speed, strict acoustic noise limits, or high torque density make smooth continuous engagement and reduced dynamic loading essential for transmission reliability
questions.explanation: The added cost of precision helical gear tooling, thrust bearings, and stiff casing is justified when operating demands exceed the dynamic and acoustic capabilities of spur gears.

application-requirement-matrix.title: 9. Industrial Application Requirement & Selection Matrix
application-requirement-matrix.description: Match the appropriate gear technology (Spur vs Helical) to 6 concrete industrial operating profiles based on explicit engineering criteria.

questions.prompt: Profile 1: Cement Clinker Low-Speed Apron Conveyor (N = 25 rpm, pitch-line velocity v = 1.2 m/s, dusty and abrasive environment, heavy shock loading, low initial capital budget, simple field maintenance required). Select gear type and primary technical justification:
options: Spur Gear — Low pitch velocity (v = 1.2 m/s) avoids noise issues; zero axial thrust simplifies bearing arrangements; rugged and economical for field maintenance
Helical Gear — High speed requires high contact ratio
Helical Gear — Axial thrust is required to clear dust from the bearing seals
Spur Gear — Must be chosen because helical gears cannot transmit torque below 100 rpm
questions.correctAnswer: Spur Gear — Low pitch velocity (v = 1.2 m/s) avoids noise issues; zero axial thrust simplifies bearing arrangements; rugged and economical for field maintenance
questions.explanation: At low velocity (1.2 m/s), dynamic impact is negligible. Spur gears provide lowest cost, simple radial bearings, and straightforward maintenance in harsh environments.

questions.prompt: Profile 2: Electric Vehicle Single-Speed Reduction Gearbox (Input motor speed N1 = 12,000 rpm, pitch-line velocity v = 25 m/s, strict passenger cabin acoustic limit < 65 dBA, high power density, compact casing envelope). Select gear type and primary technical justification:
options: Helical Gear — High pitch velocity (v = 25 m/s) and strict noise limit (< 65 dBA) mandate progressive tooth engagement and high overlap contact ratio to eliminate gear whine
Spur Gear — Simpler manufacture makes spur gears universally preferred in modern electric vehicles
Spur Gear — Low acoustic noise is naturally produced by straight teeth at 12,000 rpm
Helical Gear — Selected solely because spur gears cannot be lubricated at speeds above 1,000 rpm
questions.correctAnswer: Helical Gear — High pitch velocity (v = 25 m/s) and strict noise limit (< 65 dBA) mandate progressive tooth engagement and high overlap contact ratio to eliminate gear whine
questions.explanation: At 25 m/s and 12,000 rpm, spur gear cyclic impact would create intolerable cabin whine. Helical gears provide quiet, continuous multi-tooth engagement.

questions.prompt: Profile 3: Hand-Operated Workshop Overhead Crane Winch (Intermittent manual hand-crank operation, low rotational speed, zero high-speed noise concern, highly cost-sensitive, simple radial journal bushings). Select gear type and primary technical justification:
options: Spur Gear — Hand-powered intermittent operation has negligible dynamic excitation; zero axial thrust allows economical radial journal bushings without thrust bearings
Helical Gear — Manual hand winches require high helix angles to prevent backward rotation
Helical Gear — Tapered roller thrust bearings are mandatory for manual winches
Spur Gear — Selected solely because helical gears cannot be turned by human hand
questions.correctAnswer: Spur Gear — Hand-powered intermittent operation has negligible dynamic excitation; zero axial thrust allows economical radial journal bushings without thrust bearings
questions.explanation: Manual cranking has negligible dynamic impact. Spur gears minimize manufacturing cost and eliminate thrust forces on simple winch bushings.

questions.prompt: Profile 4: Industrial Centrifugal Process Gas Compressor (Transmitted power P = 55 kW, motor speed N1 = 2950 rpm, pitch-line velocity v = 18 m/s, continuous 24/7 chemical plant duty, high reliability required). Select gear type and primary technical justification:
options: Helical Gear — High pitch velocity (18 m/s) and continuous 24/7 duty require high Barth factor (Cv), multi-tooth load sharing, and low dynamic excitation for fatigue durability
Spur Gear — High velocity causes helical gear oil to foam, making spur gears superior
Spur Gear — Eliminates thrust bearings to minimize overall gearbox cost in chemical plants
Helical Gear — Selected because spur gears cannot transmit more than 10 kW
questions.correctAnswer: Helical Gear — High pitch velocity (18 m/s) and continuous 24/7 duty require high Barth factor (Cv), multi-tooth load sharing, and low dynamic excitation for fatigue durability
questions.explanation: At 18 m/s, spur gears suffer severe dynamic load penalties. Helical gears maintain high Cv and tooth overlap, ensuring 24/7 fatigue life in critical turbomachinery.

questions.prompt: Profile 5: Agricultural Seed Planter Ground-Wheel Metering Drive (Ground speed v < 0.5 m/s, exposed open gear drive, dirt and debris exposure, low manufacturing precision, cost-critical). Select gear type and primary technical justification:
options: Spur Gear — Very low operating speed (v < 0.5 m/s), rugged field environment, and high tolerance to axial misalignment make simple spur gears technically and economically optimal
Helical Gear — Agricultural seed metering requires precision helical lead angles to meter seeds accurately
Helical Gear — Axial thrust is required to shake excess seeds off the gear teeth
Spur Gear — Selected because helical gears cannot be manufactured in iron
questions.correctAnswer: Spur Gear — Very low operating speed (v < 0.5 m/s), rugged field environment, and high tolerance to axial misalignment make simple spur gears technically and economically optimal
questions.explanation: At sub-1 m/s ground speeds, dynamic shock is absent. Spur gears tolerate rough field conditions, open mounting, and axial shift without performance loss.

questions.prompt: Profile 6: Paper Mill Continuous Drying Cylinder Drive (Operating speed v = 14 m/s, continuous web tension, paper surface extremely sensitive to cyclic tooth impact vibration marks). Select gear type and primary technical justification:
options: Helical Gear — Smooth progressive tooth engagement eliminates cyclic impact vibration, preventing periodic chatter marks on the continuous paper web and ensuring product quality
Spur Gear — Paper web drying requires cyclic vibration pulses to shake moisture from the paper
Spur Gear — Spur teeth provide better traction on the paper drying cylinders
Helical Gear — Selected because paper drying requires non-metallic gears only
questions.correctAnswer: Helical Gear — Smooth progressive tooth engagement eliminates cyclic impact vibration, preventing periodic chatter marks on the continuous paper web and ensuring product quality
questions.explanation: Spur tooth entry shock induces torsional vibration into drying cylinders, imprinting visible chatter lines across delicate paper sheets. Helical gears ensure ripple-free torque.
